You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From a13502073638a0b28d84099fa985971fe3287aee Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Andy Shevchenko <andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2020 18:17:27 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] kgdb: Drop malformed kernel doc comment

Kernel doc does not understand POD variables to be referred to.

.../debug_core.c:73: warning: cannot understand function prototype:
'int                             kgdb_connected; '

Convert kernel doc to pure comment.

Fixes: dc7d55270521 ("kgdb: core")
Cc: Jason Wessel <jason.wessel@windriver.com>
Signed-off-by: Andy Shevchenko <andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Thompson <daniel.thompson@linaro.org>
---
 kernel/debug/debug_core.c | 4 +---
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/kernel/debug/debug_core.c b/kernel/debug/debug_core.c
index 2b7c9b67931d..2266ba27f27d 100644
--- a/kernel/debug/debug_core.c
+++ b/kernel/debug/debug_core.c
@@ -67,9 +67,7 @@ static int kgdb_break_asap;
 
 struct debuggerinfo_struct kgdb_info[NR_CPUS];
 
-/**
- * kgdb_connected - Is a host GDB connected to us?
- */
+/* kgdb_connected - Is a host GDB connected to us? */
 int				kgdb_connected;
 EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(kgdb_connected);
 
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The kernel documentation tool (kernel doc) was unable to parse the function prototype for the variable `kgdb_connected` due to its formatting as a POD (Plain Old Data) variable. The original comment was in a format that the documentation tool did not recognize, leading to a warning during the documentation generation process. The fix involved converting the kernel doc comment to a standard comment format that the documentation tool can understand.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    
    Provide a response strictly in the following format:
    Code statements:
    <text1>
    <text2>
    <text3>
    <text4>
    ...
    <textN>

Root cause:

The fix involved converting the kernel doc comment to a standard comment format that the documentation tool can understand.
